Introduction

This computational essay will about discuss the Chicago Region in the Illinois State in the United States of America. The data on the map will be plotted using information about Educational Facilities and Student Performance in the State. The maps will be generated by retrieving data through various APIs and styled using Mapbox and Choropleths. Further details about the displayed map and the reasons for the conclusions drawn, will be discussed in the writing.

Retrieving The Shape File ¶

First a shape file was retrieved from USA Government Data that contained location data about Chicago. The shape file simply contained the boudaries of each zip code and the geometry was in MULTIPOLYGON. First the CRS of the base map was set to the CRS EPSG 4326. The decison to use this crs is, according to Jurkowska (2023) due to reasons such as,

  • Being Widely Adopted in the World
  • Applicable for Global usage since it covers the Entire earth
  • Not having Disortion issues of Web Mercator

Next the Chicago shape file was simply plotted using the plot command from the matplotlib python library .

In [48]:

chicago_shape["id_str"] = chicago_shape.index.astype(str)

Retrieving Data Using APIs ¶

The data about schools and libraries were retrieved from the Chicago Data Portal. Accessing the data is completely free and can be done thorugh a simple API call by specifying the endpoint of the data needed to be retrieved. For example, https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/ykhx-yxn9.json URL enables an API call to recieve a Spatial Data Frame about schools in Chicago.

Calling Cleaning and Plotting Data About School ¶

School Data from the API ¶

The Spatial Data Frame retrieved from the API includes The 2013 School Progress Report Card data elements for each CPS high school, offering an annual summary of the school's performance. The code snippet below fetches the data through the API, converts it to String Format, and then outputs it using a for loop to get a general sense of the dataset content, helping in identifying outliers and crucial points for subsequent analysis.

Cleaning Data About School To Suit Our Analysis ¶

From the data retrieved from the API regarding high schools, only a handful of columns are deemed significant for the analysis conducted in this computational essay. These include "Name of the School", "Zip Code of School Location", "EPAS Growth Percentile", and a few others. Among these columns, one that holds paramount importance for our analysis is the "EPAS Growth Percentile". The outliers were removed and the NA values were ommited to have a constant flow in analysed data.

Importance of EPAS Growth Percentile¶

The Student Growth Percentile (SGP) is a scale used to measure academic performance of students comapred to their peers in similar academic level (Renaissance Learning, n.d). These results might help guide decisions about schooling and are frequently utilised for assessment reasons. For example, lower percentile ratings may indicate that a student needs specialised help in a given area. The outcomes of these evaluations provide teachers the ability to pinpoint particular problems that require attention and to schedule timely interventions (Logsdon, 2023). With these reasoning the analysis were decided to be carried on the Growth Percentile rate of the high schools in the region to find out the schools performance based on their students grades.

Processing data about schools. ¶

Next the data was grouped by the zip code and calculated the mean Growth Percentile for each zip code. Few reasons for using the mean value to group the data are,

  • Since mean uses the whole data for the selected variable it supports in good representation of data.(Manikandan, 2011)
  • Mean helps to measure central tendency.(Manikandan, 2011)
  • Robust and moderate against outliers.

Hence, calculating the Median Growth Percentile can provide insights into how well students have performed on average in specific zip codes. As per the New Jersey Department of Education, the Median Student Growth Percentile helps gauge the progress of groups of students, schools, areas, and classes. This serves as a valuable indicator of performance, not just for individual students, but for each school within specific zip codes. The following code snippet is to group the data by ZIPs with related to their mean.

In [51]:

Plotting the Map ¶

In [53]:
# DF to GDF
school_combined_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(school_combined_df, geometry='geometry')
vmax = school_combined_gdf['epas_attainment_percentile'].quantile(0.90)
norm = mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=school_combined_gdf['epas_attainment_percentile'].min(), vmax=vmax)

# Plotting map
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 6))  # 1 row, 2 columns

ax[0].set_axis_off()
school_combined_gdf.plot(ax=ax[0], column='epas_attainment_percentile', cmap='OrRd', legend=True, norm=norm, edgecolor='grey')
title_parameters = {'fontsize': '17', 'fontname': 'Times New Roman', 'fontweight': 'bold'}
ax[0].set_title("Mean EPAS Level in Chicago Schools", **title_parameters)

n = 2  # Display every nth zip code
ax[1].bar(average_percentile_by_zip['zip'][::n], average_percentile_by_zip['epas_attainment_percentile'][::n], color='skyblue')
ax[1].set_xlabel('Zip Codes')
ax[1].set_ylabel('Average EPAS Attainment Percentile')
ax[1].set_title('Average EPAS Attainment Percentile by Zip Code')
ax[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Analysis on the static map on Mean EPAS Level in Chicago Schools ¶

The code snippet calculates the 90th percentile (0.90 quantile) of the 'epas_attainment_percentile' column and uses this value to plot the above map. The vmax value obtained from the 90th percentile helps in setting the upper limit for colour normalization, ensuring that the map highlights areas with higher attainment levels while maintaining variation in the data.

As it can be obveserved in the map there is quite a good variation/ spread of how students of school perform in different zip codes. The upper area of Chicago seems to have schools that tend to perform well based on the Mean Growth Percentile Level suggesting the majority of well performing schools tend to be in those specific zip codes. The bar chart represents Average EPAS Attainment Percentile by Zip Code for every nth zip code. {Did not plot every zip code to minimze clutter.}

Accoring the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (2016), performance of these schools in specific regions can be dependent on several factors such as,

  • Safe and Supportive Environment.
  • Infrastructures and Facilites around the Area
  • Cultural Emphasis within the area

Well-maintained infrastructure providing comfortable, quiet study spaces with readily available resources can significantly enhance the learning experience for students, fostering academic engagement and potentially leading to improved academic performance. When speaking on educational infrastructure the first things pops up to ones mind is having good library facilities.

Libraries offer vital resources, support networks, and a stimulating atmosphere that may both directly and indirectly raise student achievement. They are an integral aspect of the educational infrastructure. Libraries handle resource constraints, provide concentrated study places, encourage literacy, and give instructional assistance in order to help students succeed in a variety of academic subjects (Lance & E. Kachel, 2023).

Therefore the decission was taken to see the relationship on how infrastructure fascilites such as libraries improve student Performance. With that reasoning the following steps explained the computational essay was carried out.

The Spatial Data Frame retrieved from the API includes Total library visitors in Chicago for the Year 2023 The code snippet below fetches the data through the API, converts it to String Format. The total number of visitors to the library reflects the actual library visitors, not the foot traffic or visitors in the vicinity.

Cleaning Data About Libraries To Suit Our Analysis ¶

From the json data received from the above API call it is important to extract the data that will be needed for our analysis. After converting the data into pandas dataframe it was observed that the latitude and the longitude was not directly available as a columm. Therfore, they were put into columns the outlier columns were dropped and the NA values were discarded to have a clean dataframe that will help for a clean analysis to be carried out. The relevant steps are conducted using the below code snippet.

After cleaning the dataframe will contain information such as "branch name", "address", "zip", "visitors per each month", "latitude and longitude coordinates" about different libraries in Chicago.

In [55]:
library_data_df = pd.DataFrame(library_data)

# Latitude Longitude not in correct order . Ectracting them from the json and putting them into seperate columns
library_data_df['latitude'] = library_data_df['location'].apply(lambda loc: loc.get('coordinates')[1] if loc else None)
library_data_df['longitude'] = library_data_df['location'].apply(lambda loc: loc.get('coordinates')[0] if loc else None)

#Computed region data not needed. The locsation data cn be removed because the latitude and longitude was extracted.
prefix_to_drop = ':@computed_region'
columns_to_drop = [col for col in library_data_df.columns if col.startswith(prefix_to_drop)]
library_data_cleaned_df = library_data_df.drop(columns=columns_to_drop, errors='ignore')
library_data_cleaned_df = library_data_cleaned_df.drop(columns="location", errors='ignore')

Processing data about libraries. ¶

Getting Total Number Visitors Per Each Library ¶

Since the filtered original data frame already contains information on library visitors per month, it is essential to determine the total visitors per library for the year 2022. Several reasons can be cited to explain what draws more visitors to libraries (Rasmussen, 2019):

  1. The availability of physical materials like books and multimedia resources.
  2. Access to digital resources such as online databases and eBooks.
  3. Quiet and conducive study spaces that enhance the student experience.
These and other features can attract more students, offering them an enhanced educational experience that can lead to better performance and higher scores, consequently driving the Growth Percentile of regions. Nonetheless, this is not always the case, and as we progress through the computational essay, more insights will be shared regarding these factors.
In [56]:

library_data_cleaned_df[months] = library_data_cleaned_df[months].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors='coerce')

# Insert sum of total visitors for 12months per each branch into a new column

When examining the above plotted maps, it is evident that they exhibit a similar pattern, indicating a correlation between the Growth Percentile of students and Total Visitors of Libraries. In both maps, the darker regions typically correspond to higher values based on the selected color palettes. Specifically, considering the map illustrating the Growth Percentile of Students on the left, the zip codes with higher numbers (darker colors) align with the same zips in the map displaying Total library visitors by zip code on the right, showing darker hues.

However, there are some zips that do not approve with the above mentioned conclusion.Therefore before continuing further analysis it was necessary to confirm whether the majority of the zips followed the foresaid conclusion of Regions with Higher Growth Percentiles Have Libraries with Higher Number of Annual Visitors. Inorder to prove the validity the following scatter plot was constructed.

Analysing the scatter plot it is prominent that zips with low Growth Percentile corresponds with the zips which has libraries with lower number of visitors proving the conclusion discussed above.

    threshold_scale=[school_combined_df["epas_attainment_percentile"].quantile(q=i/7) for i in range(8)],
).add_to(chicago_map)

About the initial map ¶

The map basically displays the Mean Growth Percentile for each zip code. With the use of the tooltip an observer can get to know the Mean Growth Percentile of the polygon their toggling with. Also the map highlights the current toggling polygon. The reason for choosing few settings of the map are as follows.

  1. The Threshold Scale is used to display the data values by segmenting the data to 8 segments. By computing quantile values for the "epas_attainment_percentile" column in the DataFrame named `school_combined_df`, it populates the list with these calculated values.
  2. The `YlOrRd` colour pallette was used. So that it will give zip codes with schools that had higher mean growth percentile more attention. And the light colors viceversa.
  3. Zoom level was set to '9.5' so that it would give a clear inital view of the region.

from folium.plugins import MarkerCluster
# Define a function to assign colors based on total visitors
def assign_color(total_visitors):
    if total_visitors < 33000:
        return 'green'  # Low
    elif 10000 <= total_visitors < 43000:
        return 'orange'  # Mid
    else:
        return 'red'  # High
        
# Create a MarkerCluster to group nearby markers
marker_cluster = MarkerCluster().add_to(chicago_map)

for index, row in library_data_dropped_df.iterrows():
    location_coordinates = (row['latitude'], row['longitude'])
    
    # Use the assign_color function to determine the marker color
    marker_color = assign_color(row['total_visitors_per_year'])
    
    library_icon = folium.Icon(icon='book', prefix='fa', color=marker_color)

    # Customize the popup content with branch name, total visitors, and address
    popup_content = f"<div style='width: 200px;'><b>Branch Name:</b> {row['branch']}<br>" \
                    f"<b>Total Visitors Per Year:</b> {row['total_visitors_per_year']}<br>" \
                    f"<b>Address:</b> {row['address']}</div>"

   
    folium.Marker(location=location_coordinates, popup=popup_content, icon=library_icon).add_to(marker_cluster)

Brief on Previous Actions ¶

Zip codes were filtered to provide information on the two lowest zip codes where the majority of high schools had low Mean Growth Percentile and plotted on the map. The tooltips will help viewers identify about each marker represents.

Utlising another API ¶

The number of visotrs of to a public library depend on few factors. According to a report by loes for livet , follwing are few of those many reasons,

  • Library being too far away and students cannot easily commute to travel.
  • Not understanding the library Environment.
  • Students not understanding the value of the fascilities.

It was decided to investigate whether there is a correlation between students visiting the library and the distance to it based on the aforementioned reasons. To determine this, the distance from the centroid of ZIP codes with the two lowest Mean Growth Percentile to their nearest library from the top 5 libraries with the highest number of visitors in 2022 was calculated using the Open Route Service API. After finding the nearest library for both the zip codes the path to that library was plotted for better visualisation of what travel methods can be used. it is worthwhile to notice the path drawn is not merely a line drawn between two points instead the actual shortest path that students can use to commute to libraries. This can be further verified by zooming on the plotted paths.

Function to Plot the Path and Display the Distance ¶

In [67]:
def draw_path_and_labels(api_response, map_obj):
    # Function to style the GeoJson layer for the route
    def style_function(feature):
        return {
            "color": "blue", 
        }

    coordinates = api_response['features'][0]['geometry']['coordinates']

    # Reverse the order of coordinates so that it can be plotted in folium because the api return lot lan
    reversed_coordinates = [(lat, lon) for lon, lat in coordinates]
    polyline = folium.PolyLine(
        locations=reversed_coordinates,
        color='blue',
        weight=5,  
        opacity=1,  
    ).add_to(map_obj)

    # ADrawing Polylines for each segment
    for i, coord in enumerate(reversed_coordinates[:-1]):
        if i < len(api_response['features'][0]['properties']['segments']): #accessing the necessary column
            distance_segment = api_response['features'][0]['properties']['segments'][i]['distance']
            #meters into km API gave me meters
            popup_content = f"Distance: {distance_segment / 1000:.2f} km"
            popup_options = {'offset': (0, -20), 'zIndex': 1000} 
            label = folium.Marker(
                
                location=coord,
                icon=folium.DivIcon(
                    icon_size=(150,36),
                    icon_anchor=(7,20),
                    html=f"<div style='background-color:white; padding: 5px;'>{popup_content}</div>"
                )
            )
            label.add_to(map_obj)

    return

The Final Analysis and the Conclusion ¶

Throughout this computational essay, several key factors have been carefully examined:

  1. The Definition and Importance of Growth Percentile in Evaluating Student Performance in the High Schools of Chicago.
  2. Mapping the Mean Growth Percentile per zip code to visualize the distribution.
  3. Exploring the factors contributing to increased visitor numbers in libraries.
  4. Investigating the correlation between libraries with higher visitor counts and schools with higher Mean Growth Percentile.
  5. Exploring potential reasons for libraries not attracting visitors as expected.
  6. Validating the accuracy of one of the reasons identified.
  7. Visualizing all these insights on a single map to narrate a cohesive story.

The story conveyed by the final map ¶

The polygons on the map shows the distribution of the Mean Growth Percentile per zip code and the map is plotted by using quantile values to show an equal distribution . The markers with a book icon represents the Top 5 Libraries by visiotrs and the school icon ZIP Codes with lowest Mean Growth Percentile.

Observations ¶

Majority of the libraries that have a higher number of total visitors are situated in the zip codes with a higher number of schools, resulting in a higher Mean Growth Percentile (shown in darker color polygons). This observation aligns perfectly with the scatter plot discussed earlier in this write-up. Also this can be proven by zooming into zip codes with lower Mean Growth Percentile where the viewer will be able to see there is either no library in that zip or there is a library with not much visitors.

Continuing, it was previously discussed that the distance from a zip code to the libraries may affect students' performance. Let's further dive into this argument by revisiting the key points highlighted throughout this essay:

  1. For libraries to attract a good number of visitors, they should provide excellent facilities.
  2. Students benefit from having access to good library facilities, leading to improved academic performance and a higher Mean Growth Percentile.
  3. A significant reason why students may not utilize libraries is the distance they have to travel to reach them.

Therefore, as observed, the zip codes with the lowest performance have a considerable distance to the nearest library with good reputation and facilities. This lack of access to enhanced study experiences could be a contributing factor to the lower Mean Growth Percentile seen in these zip codes.

In conclusion, it is imperative for the municipalities of Chicago to either build better library facilities evenly distributed across all zip codes or establish affordable, efficient, and convenient public transportation systems to enable students to reach better libraries. This strategic approach could lead to improved student performance, consequently boosting the Mean Growth Percentile across Chicago.
